newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Sept PPI up 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Sept PPI up 0.2 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department said the September Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 0.2 percent, following a 0.3-percent increase in August.

The core rate, which excludes volatile food and energy items, was up 0.3 percent. U.S. economists in a Reuters survey had expected 0.3-percent rise in the overall rate and a 0.2 pct rise in the core rate.
CHERYL KATZ, SENIOR ECONOMIST, MERRILL LYNCH: "It's obvious that the core PPI was boosted by a 1.2-percent rise in car prices.
September is always a pretty funny month. That will most likely not be repeated next month, so I wouldn't get too excited about that."

ROBERT DEDERICK, ECONOMIC CONSULTANT, NORTHERN TRUST CO: "The basic thing was the automobile phenomenon, because of the end of the model year. When you take that number out of there, it's up only 0.1 (percent). This is not the kind of thing to take fright at.
"There's a little hint out there that the decline at the intermediate goods level is behind us now. Perhaps the expansion is having a small price impact, but that might be mining the data too deeply.
"The important thing is as of now, inflation remains well-contained at the producer level."

ROBERT BRUSCA, CHIEF ECONOMIST, NIKKO SECURITIES CO: "Energy prices are still going up, but over-to-date, core PPI is up only 1.4 percent. The inflation story is going to be the Consumer Price Index," Brusca said.

"We are seeing tremendous productivity results in the goods-producing sector... Even if there is any pressure from commodities or wages, that sector can grind it out. However, productivity is a lot lower in services so that wage pressures hit there first."
WALDO BEST, SENIOR ECONOMIST, BZW GOVERNMENT SECURITIES: "Of these morning's numbers I think the PPI is what is really driving some buyers into the (domestic money) market.

"We knew that the core (rate) would start to pick up due to stronger hourly earnings earlier in the year. It's a very neutral number and there's really no big surprise. But it does signal that next week's CPI will probably be a benign number as well.
"I think we'll see a bit of a relief rally today (in the money market) that can continue into next week."
